mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in FEDFUNDS predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in <50% of triggered instances despite negative FEDFUNDS trend (p >0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A crossing of FEDFUNDS above 4.5% triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly negative (p >0.05) despite FEDFUNDS crossing above 4.5% in a tightening regime.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rise in GDPC1 (demand) above 2.5% and UNRATE below 4.0% triggers positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly positive (p >0.05) despite meeting the trigger condition in an expanding economy.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a sustained decline in FEDFUNDS predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly positive (p >0.05) in late-cycle expansion despite FEDFUNDS decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO (supply) above 5% predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly positive (p >0.05) over 60 days despite INDPRO rise above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly rises in GDPC1 (demand) above 2.5% and INDPRO (supply) above 5% trigger positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly positive (p >0.05) despite meeting the trigger condition in an expanding economy.

mechanism_narrative: A crossing of UNRATE below 4.0% triggers positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly positive (p >0.05) over 5 days despite UNRATE falling below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle regime, a rise in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly negative (p >0.05) despite FEDFUNDS rise above 4.5% in a tightening regime.
